about: One case or more for each rule of ADR 038 decision 33 (R1–R26), and for each row of decision 34 one or more marked `reading` with the row's number (1–11, in the table's order), written by hand from the ADR's text — never by scripts/domino-oracle/make.py, which only replays them. README.md beside the script has the format.

cases.name: the 28 tiles 0-0 … 6-6, a tile's pips the sum of its numbers, seven doubles
seven tiles a seat; the boneyard 14 at two, 7 at three, none at four and pairs; at pairs 0 and 2 against 1 and 3
turns go round the seats in their order, one tile a turn
five doubles in one hand: dealt again
five tiles of one number, its double not counted: dealt again
four doubles and four tiles of a number in one hand: the deal stands
reading: five of the six tiles that pair 3 with another, beside 3-3, is dealt again — the double is not counted either way
reading: four of 3 beside 3-3 — five with the double — stands
reading: a deal R4 throws is dealt again before anyone sees it — the hand is the first try that stands
at pairs, no opponent of the first tile's player can answer it: the hand is void, and with an account open the same seat opens again
one opponent's answer is enough: the hand goes on
reading: the first tile's play stands as an act, the hand is void, and the next deal finds the opener again
while no account is open the lowest double held opens, with it; 0-0 is not counted
no seat holds 1-1 … 6-6: the seat with the lowest tile opens with it, and nobody draws
reading: the standard list — the lowest tile opens, nobody draws for a double (an opening draw would have given seat 0 the 1-1)
reading: of two tiles with the same pips the one whose larger number is smaller — 2-1 before 3-0
reading: 0-0, when a seat holds it, is the lowest tile
(a) once an account is open the seat that finished opens with any tile it holds; the first tile lies as written, its larger number at the left
(b) after a blocked hand the seat with the fewest pips opens, whichever its side
(c) after a tied hand the seat that made its last play opens
reading: of seats with the same fewest pips, one of the winning side first — seat 3 before seat 2, though seat 2 comes first in the turns from the last player
«Sən aç»: the seat with the right gives the opening to its partner, who opens with any tile and cannot give it back
under R6 nobody gives
a tile goes to the end whose number it matches and that end shows its other number; a double is one tile; where both ends show one number the left alone is listed
a seat that holds a fitting tile plays: no draw, the boneyard as it was
a seat without a fitting tile draws two at a time until it holds one — the pair is drawn whole — and then plays
it draws until two are left, never the last two, and passes when nothing fits
reading: with three left a seat draws one — a boneyard of seven goes 7, 5, 3, 2
while only a double could fit an end nobody draws: the seats pass and the hand is blocked with 6-6 still in the boneyard
reading: the closed boneyard is a fact of the line alone; a seat that holds the double still plays it
a seat with no fitting tile and nothing to draw passes, and the next seat plays
a hand ends when a seat plays its last tile
a hand ends blocked when no seat can play and none may draw
a hand that holds 0-0 alone counts 10
0-0 beside another tile counts nothing
the finisher's side gains the pips of the other side's seats exactly; the partner's are not counted
at two the finisher gains the other seat's pips, a lone 0-0's 10 among them
blocked: the one side with the lowest count gains the counts of all the others
the boneyard counts for nobody
two sides share the lowest count: nobody wins the hand
the tie's pips — every seat's — go to the bank
reading: at three sides any tie for the lowest count is a tie
accounts begin closed at 0 with nothing waiting and no tries, the bank empty; an open account adds its gain
a closed account opens with a gain of 13 or more, which takes its waiting points with it; 12 waits
a closed winner under 13 waits, one try more; at its third try its waiting points burn, the third gain with them; another side's win in between changes no count
reading: after the burn the tries start again from none — three more before the next
a win of an open account — the opening hand included — burns the closed accounts' waiting points; a closed winner burns nobody's
ties add to the bank; a winner whose account is open, or opens in that hand, takes it
the bank does not count toward 13, and burns with a winner whose account stays closed
the game ends when a balance is 101 or more, by a blocked hand too; waiting points and the bank are no part of a balance
a dry win: every other side's balance is 0 at the end
not dry: the other side opened its account
reading: at three sides a win is dry when every other side is at 0
reading: at three sides one other side above 0 is enough to make it no dry win
